title: Variables: Declaration, Initialization, and Typing Discipline
description: How variable declaration, initialization, and static vs. dynamic typing differ across the three languages.
objectives: Compare dynamic vs. static typing at the variable level

content.heading: Python
content.body: Variables need no declared type — a name simply comes into existence the moment it's assigned: x = 5. There's no way to 'declare but not initialize' a variable in the C/Java sense; reading a name before it's ever been assigned raises a NameError. The same name can be rebound to a completely different type later.

content.heading: Java
content.body: Local variables must be declared with an explicit type (or var, for compiler-inferred typing) and must be definitely assigned before use — reading an unassigned local variable is a compile error. Instance/class fields, if not explicitly initialized, get automatic defaults (0, false, null).

content.heading: C
content.body: Variables must be declared with an explicit type. Local variables are NOT automatically initialized — reading one before assignment yields indeterminate garbage (undefined behavior), a sharp contrast to Java's compile-time enforcement. Global variables do get automatic zero-initialization, similar to Java's fields.

content.heading: Key Differences
content.body: Python needs no type declaration at all and rebinds names dynamically. Java requires a declared (or inferred) type and enforces at compile time that locals are assigned before use. C requires a declared type but does NOT enforce initialization for locals — an uninitialized local variable is a live bug waiting to happen, not a caught error.

content.heading: When It Matters
content.body: This is one of the starkest safety differences among the three: a C program can silently misbehave from an uninitialized variable, something both Java (compile-time check) and Python (no uninitialized state possible) prevent by construction.

keyPoints: Python: no type declaration, dynamic rebinding, no uninitialized-variable state is possible
Java: explicit (or inferred) type, compiler enforces locals are assigned before use
C: explicit type required, but local variable initialization is NOT enforced — a real safety gap
